citations.summary: For the Wilson lattice action with gauge fields and Wilson fermions, the paper proves non-negativity of the reflected correlation for every gauge-invariant observable in the designated positive half-space, including reflections through site-containing planes; the fermionic statement assumes hopping parameter K < 1/6.

formulas.statement: For every gauge-invariant F supported in the stated positive region, the normalized Wilson expectation of Theta(F)F is nonnegative, under the stated Wilson-fermion assumptions.
formulas.exactness: paraphrase of Eq. (2.4) with its adjacent hypotheses

lean_targets: future SU(2) Wilson reflection-positivity producer artefact
use_for: Site-plane versus link-plane reflection distinction.
Gauge-invariant-observable scope.
Required antilinearity and complex conjugation under reflection.
Wilson-action-specific reflected factorisation architecture.
do_not_use_for: A proof that this repository's SU(2) splitting identity is correct.
A continuum limit.
A mass gap.
Removal of the K < 1/6 assumption in the paper's fermionic model without separately taking the pure-gauge specialization.
open_questions: The future producer must exhibit its own lattice geometry, boundary classification, Haar normalisation, and gluing identity; citation alone does not discharge them.

citations.summary: On a finite four-dimensional Wilson lattice with gauge group SU(N), Lüscher constructs the physical Hilbert space and transfer matrix. Proposition 1 states that T is bounded, self-adjoint, gauge invariant, and strictly positive. The one-link kernel is expanded in irreducible characters; strict positivity is equivalent to positive coefficients, obtained from tensor-product multiplicities. Proposition 2 identifies the Euclidean expectations with operator Schwinger functions under the stated boundary conditions.

formulas.statement: The transfer matrix is self-adjoint, bounded, gauge invariant under the stated transformations, and strictly positive; the Hamiltonian is H = -(1/a) log T.
The relevant central one-link kernel has an irreducible-character expansion, and positivity of its quadratic form is necessary and sufficient for every character coefficient to be positive.
formulas.ascii: K(V) = sum_r c_r chi_r(V), with c_r > 0

use_for: SU(N), hence SU(2), character-coefficient positivity test.
Haar-based one-link quadratic form.
Null quotient/completion and one-step time translation.
The physical units H = -(1/a) log T.
Exact separation between infinite-volume lattice and continuum scaling.
do_not_use_for: Automatic continuum reconstruction.
Vacuum uniqueness: the paper explicitly says it is not known there.
Boundary-condition independence.
A positive physical mass uniform in a or volume.
open_questions: A producer must match its character and Haar conventions to Eq. (23), including any dimension factors.
A claimed continuum mass must control the spectrum after the factor 1/a and all regulator limits.

citations.summary: The paper distinguishes sending the finite lattice extents M,L to infinity, which produces the infinite-volume lattice theory, from a continuum theory obtained only through a further large-distance/critical limit with bare parameters near critical values.
extracted_claims: M,L -> infinity is identified as the infinite-volume lattice theory; the continuum theory is described as a separate critical/large-distance limit.
use_for: Rejecting the identification of a thermodynamic limit at fixed lattice regulator with a continuum limit.
do_not_use_for: Existence of the critical limit.
Nontriviality of a continuum theory.

citations.summary: OS I formulates E0 temperedness, E1 Euclidean covariance, E2 positivity, E3 symmetry, and E4 cluster, and states an E-to-R reconstruction theorem. OS II later reports that a lemma in this proof is wrong and that sufficiency of this original E0-E4 package is open.

formulas.statement: The original Euclidean package is E0 temperedness, E1 Euclidean covariance, E2 positivity, E3 symmetry, and E4 cluster.

use_for: Historical definition of the OS axiom labels.
Showing that reflection positivity alone is only E2.
do_not_use_for: Sufficiency of the unmodified original E0-E4 assumptions; OS II corrects this point.
Lattice transfer-matrix positivity without the extra lattice argument.

citations.summary: OS II corrects OS I. Its main reconstruction theorem requires the stronger E0' linear-growth condition (or E0'') together with E1-E4. It then yields a unique Wightman theory satisfying R0-R5 and the additional R0' growth property.

formulas.statement: A sequence satisfying E0' (or E0'') and E1-E4 is the Euclidean Green-function sequence of a uniquely determined Wightman QFT; the Wightman distributions satisfy R0-R5 and R0'.
formulas.ascii: E0' (or E0'') + E1-E4 => unique Wightman QFT with R0-R5 and R0'
formulas.exactness: Theorem E' (or E'') -> R' on printed page 287

use_for: The real hypotheses of corrected continuum OS reconstruction.
Distinguishing reflection positivity from full Wightman reconstruction.
Requiring regularity/growth, Euclidean covariance, symmetry, and cluster assumptions in addition to positivity.
do_not_use_for: Claiming that finite-lattice reflection positivity alone constructs a continuum Wightman QFT.
Claiming a mass gap; the theorem reconstructs a QFT but does not supply a positive gap.
open_questions: A producer must state which precise version of the growth condition is proved for its Schwinger functions.

citations.summary: The official problem asks, for every compact simple gauge group G, for a nontrivial quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 with axiomatic properties at least as strong as the cited Wightman/OS requirements and with a mass gap Delta > 0, meaning no Hamiltonian spectrum in (0,Delta).

formulas.statement: For every compact simple G, prove existence of a nontrivial quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 with a mass gap Delta > 0 and axiomatic properties at least as strong as the cited schemes.
formulas.ascii: forall compact simple G, exists nontrivial QYM on R^4 with gap Delta > 0
formulas.exactness: faithful paraphrase of the official boxed problem statement

use_for: The exact external standard for Clay comparison.
The spectral definition of the mass gap.
The required nontriviality and R^4 setting.
do_not_use_for: Turning a repository percentage into a mathematical estimate.
Crediting a finite-lattice, fixed-a, conditional, or abelian result as the Clay result.

citations.summary: The official description separates compact/finite approximations from R^4, makes uniform estimates central, explains cutoff- and volume-dependent renormalisation in constructive limits, requires a non-Gaussian measure for nonlinear fields, requires both a->0 and volume->infinity for the Wilson lattice route, and explicitly excludes weak existence by compactness unless properties of the limit such as axioms and a mass gap are also established.
extracted_claims: For the Wilson lattice route one must verify limits as lattice spacing tends to zero and volume tends to infinity.
Weak existence by compactness is explicitly excluded as a solution unless properties of the limit, including axioms and a mass gap, are also established.
A non-Gaussian Euclidean measure is required to obtain a nonlinear field in the scalar example used to explain nontriviality.
use_for: Regulator and limit-order audit.
Renormalisation-dependence audit.
Nontriviality and Gaussian-limit audit.
Rejecting compactness alone as a Clay solution.
Requiring uniform-in-volume mass-gap control for the R^4 route.
do_not_use_for: A ready-made tightness theorem in a producer's chosen topology.
A substitute for proving convergence, uniqueness, OS axioms, nontriviality, or a mass gap.
open_questions: CONT-C0 must specify its actual topology and observables; the official description does not choose them for the producer.
